recommendations.title: The Midnight Disease
recommendations.author: Alice Flaherty
recommendations.reason: Their interest in science, psychology, and literary fiction (The Pale King, The Bell Jar, Chaos) suggests they'd appreciate this neurologist's exploration of the compulsion to write and the brain's role in creativity.

recommendations.title: Mexican Gothic
recommendations.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
recommendations.reason: Their list shows a strong appetite for gothic horror with literary ambition (The Haunting of Hill House, Rebecca, Silver Nitrate already read; Dark Matter, The September House on their list), and Moreno-Garcia delivers exactly that blend with a distinctive mid-century Mexican setting.

recommendations.title: The Power of the Dog
recommendations.author: Thomas Savage
recommendations.reason: Their interest in literary fiction with dark psychological undercurrents (Blood Meridian, East of Eden already read; Cottonmouths, Joe, Bull Mountain on or read) points to this devastating character study of repression and violence in the American West.

recommendations.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
recommendations.author: Amor Towles
recommendations.reason: Their taste for sweeping, elegant literary historical fiction (The Books of Jacob, The Marriage Portrait, Augustus) suggests they'd be captivated by this richly detailed novel of a Russian count living under house arrest across decades of Soviet history.

recommendations.title: The Raw Shark Texts
recommendations.author: Steven Hall
recommendations.reason: Their affinity for formally inventive, mind-bending fiction (House of Leaves already read; How to Live Safely in a Science Fictional Universe, Cloud Cuckoo Land on their list) makes this typographically experimental thriller about a man hunted by a conceptual shark an ideal fit.

recommendations.title: Last and First Men
recommendations.author: Olaf Stapledon
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list reveals a deep interest in ambitious, ideas-driven science fiction spanning cosmic scales (Hyperion, Leviathan Wakes, Contact, Solaris), and Stapledon's visionary two-billion-year history of humanity is the foundational text behind much of what they already love.

recommendations.title: The Secret House
recommendations.author: David Bodanis
recommendations.reason: Their broad curiosity spanning popular science, nonfiction, and the hidden mechanics of reality (Chaos, The Elegant Universe, Entangled Life) makes this microscopically detailed portrait of a single house over 24 hours a natural and delightful fit.

recommendations.author: Alena Graedon
recommendations.reason: Their interest in dystopian literary fiction like The Deluge, The Circle, and Parable of the Talents makes this inventive near-future thriller about the collapse of language and meaning a natural and compelling fit.

recommendations.title: Carmen Dog
recommendations.author: Carol Emshwiller
recommendations.reason: Their affinity for strange, boundary-pushing speculative fiction like How to Live Safely in a Science Fictional Universe and The Employees makes this darkly comic feminist fable about animals transforming into women a perfect offbeat discovery.

recommendations.title: The Locked Door
recommendations.author: Freida McFadden
recommendations.reason: Fans of psychological thrillers like Gone Girl and The Silent Patient will appreciate this tense, twisty narrative that blends mystery with dark secrets, matching the thriller and crime fiction heavily represented in their list.

recommendations.title: Mexican Gothic
recommendations.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
recommendations.reason: Given their love of gothic horror and atmospheric fiction from authors like Shirley Jackson and Laura Purcell, this lush, creepy novel set in 1950s Mexico delivers the same eerie, literary dread they clearly enjoy.

recommendations.title: Paul Takes the Form of a Mortal Girl
recommendations.author: Andrea Lawlor
recommendations.reason: Given their interest in LGBTQ+ fiction, literary experimentation, and books like Tipping the Velvet and Carol, this shape-shifting, playful, queer literary novel offers the same boundary-pushing storytelling they gravitate toward.

recommendations.title: Lathe of Heaven
recommendations.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list is dense with literary science fiction like Solaris, Bewilderment, and Hyperion, and Le Guin's meditative novel about dreams reshaping reality fits that same thoughtful, philosophical sci-fi tradition perfectly.

recommendations.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
recommendations.author: Amor Towles
recommendations.reason: Their list includes richly historical and literary fiction like The Books of Jacob, Augustus, and Fingersmith, and this elegant, witty novel about a Russian count under house arrest delivers the same immersive, character-driven historical storytelling.

recommendations.title: The Raw Shark Texts
recommendations.author: Steven Hall
recommendations.reason: Their taste for metafictional, genre-blending work like House of Leaves and Cloud Cuckoo Land makes this inventive literary thriller about a man hunted by a conceptual shark a compelling and natural next read.

recommendations.title: Mexican Gothic
recommendations.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
recommendations.reason: Given their interest in atmospheric gothic horror by authors like Laura Purcell and Catriona Ward, plus Silver Nitrate already read, Moreno-Garcia's lush horror novel set in 1950s Mexico is a natural fit.

recommendations.title: The Dispossessed
recommendations.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list is rich with dystopian and political science fiction like Parable of the Talents, The Deluge, and Chain-Gang All-Stars, making Le Guin's anarchist utopia novel an essential match.

recommendations.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
recommendations.author: Amor Towles
recommendations.reason: Their interest in sweeping literary historical fiction — The Books of Jacob, The Thousand Autumns of Jacob de Zoet, Fingersmith — suggests they would love this elegant, character-driven novel set across decades in a Moscow hotel.

recommendations.title: The Raw Shark Texts
recommendations.author: Steven Hall
recommendations.reason: Their appetite for formally inventive, genre-blurring fiction like House of Leaves already read and Cloud Cuckoo Land on their list makes this experimental thriller about a man hunted by a conceptual shark a compelling fit.

recommendations.title: The Children of Men
recommendations.author: P.D. James
recommendations.reason: Their extensive interest in dystopian literary fiction — from Parable of the Talents to The Light Pirate to Bewilderment — makes this quietly devastating novel about a world without human fertility an ideal match.

recommendations.title: Sabriel
recommendations.author: Garth Nix
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list spans from epic fantasy like The Way of Kings to darker fantasy like The Blacktongue Thief, and this inventive necromancer fantasy with genuine atmosphere and world-building fits that sensibility perfectly.

recommendations.title: The Historian
recommendations.author: Elizabeth Kostova
recommendations.reason: Their taste for atmospheric, literary horror and historical fiction — seen in books like Fingersmith, The Books of Jacob, and The Lamplighters — aligns closely with this richly researched gothic novel tracing Dracula across centuries.

recommendations.title: Remainder
recommendations.author: Tom McCarthy
recommendations.reason: Their interest in formally experimental literary fiction like The Pale King and No One Is Talking About This, combined with their appetite for psychologically unsettling narratives, makes this strange, obsessive novel about re-enactment a strong fit.

recommendations.title: The Haunting of Alma Fielding
recommendations.author: Kate Summerscale
recommendations.reason: Their interest in gothic horror, historical fiction, and true crime (Columbine, In Cold Blood, Dark Wire) combined with their love of Shirley Jackson-adjacent supernatural fiction makes this true story of a 1930s haunting investigation a natural fit.

recommendations.title: Mexican Gothic
recommendations.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
recommendations.reason: Given their enjoyment of Silver Nitrate by Moreno-Garcia and their strong appetite for gothic horror, literary fiction, and historical settings, this atmospheric haunted-house novel set in 1950s Mexico is an obvious next step.

recommendations.title: Plain Bad Heroines
recommendations.author: Emily M. Danforth
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list features gothic horror, LGBTQ+ fiction, and literary novels with dark edges (Our Wives Under the Sea, The Last House on Needless Street, Summer Sons), and this dual-timeline sapphic horror novel hits all those notes with sharp, witty prose.

recommendations.title: Faithful Place
recommendations.author: Tana French
recommendations.reason: They have read In the Woods and Broken Harbor and have The Searcher on their want-to-read list, making this Dublin Murder Squad entry — a deeply personal, literary crime novel about family secrets and class — essential reading in the series.

recommendations.title: Every Dead Thing
recommendations.author: John Connolly
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list shows a clear appetite for dark fiction blending supernatural horror with crime and mystery (Last Days, Dead Beat, The Only Good Indians), and this first Charlie Parker novel delivers exactly that combination with literary depth.

recommendations.title: The Worm and His Kings
recommendations.author: Hailey Piper
recommendations.reason: Their taste for visceral, LGBTQ+-inflected horror with literary ambitions (Manhunt, What Moves the Dead, Our Wives Under the Sea) aligns perfectly with this cosmic horror novella featuring a trans protagonist navigating a monstrous underground world.

recommendations.title: The Raw Shark Texts
recommendations.author: Steven Hall
recommendations.reason: Their interest in mind-bending literary fiction that plays with structure and reality (House of Leaves, Recursion, Cloud Cuckoo Land) and their taste for conceptually daring novels makes this story of a man hunted by a conceptual shark a compelling fit.

recommendations.title: The Devotion of Suspect X
recommendations.author: Keigo Higashino
recommendations.reason: Their strong pattern of reading literary crime fiction with psychological depth and moral complexity (Tana French, Patricia Highsmith, Kate Atkinson) makes this Japanese inverted mystery — focused on how rather than who — a natural recommendation.
